## FACT round-28 #1 — METHOD-LOCALITY (paper 95, /tmp/exp_methodlocality.py, /tmp/r28n1b.log)

**Verdict name: THE-METHODS-ARE-FACTOR-LOCAL.**

### Result
ECM calibrated onto the plane for the first time, and the method stratum's internal structure measured: **ρ and ECM are factor-local** (cost determined by a factor p, not by N); trial division is not.

**H1 factor-locality at medians** (fixed p = 4093, q growing 2¹⁴ → 2²³, 9 draws/cell): median flatness over 2²³ cofactor growth — **ECM ×2.16, ρ ×1.40** (flat within method luck: ECM curve-restart scatter; ρ Poisson around √p ≈ 64).

**H2/H3 p-scaling**, corrected slopes per log₂p (the script's slope print took log₂ of bit-lengths — disclosed, corrected from the printed medians):
- Pollard ρ: **0.45** — the birthday bound √p ✓
- trial division: **1.09** — linear in p, the definition face ✓
- ECM: **1.13** — locally power-like but constant-advantaged: at p = 2¹⁴ ECM needs 6 657 ops vs trial-div's 12 142 — already ahead, with sub-exponential bending beyond this window

### Method ledger
The first single-draw design was statistically inadequate (ρ's cost spans 9–136 iters per cell — flatness ratios compared single lucky/unlucky draws) → 9-draw medians before any claim. Catalog scan same round: one new relevant entry (#856 Berggren causal set, no factorization claim).

Now 430 experiments. Assessment v206. Paper 95.

explain the boundary.

### Stage 5 — Synthesize (team: Principal Investigator)

concept.title: FACT round-27 #4 — BATTERY-SCALING: the capacity curve saturates at the label-entropy ceiling (paper 94)
concept.concept_description:
## FACT round-27 #4 — BATTERY-SCALING (paper 94, /tmp/exp_batteryscaling.py, /tmp/r27n4b.log)

**Verdict name: THE-CURVE-SATURATES-AT-THE-CEILING.**

### Result
The battery extended to **six dials** (adding F₂₀ x⁵−2 @5 and C₅ Q(ζ₁₁)⁺ @11; all conductors pairwise coprime, CRT modulus 31·23·9·8·5·11). The nested-subset capacity curve:

| dials | I(joint) | Σ marginals | deficit | ceiling | % of ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.0011 | 1.0011 | +0.000 | — | — |
| 2 | 2.1334 | 2.0020 | +0.132 | 4.6063 | 46% |
| 3 | 4.0242 | 2.4777 | +1.547 | 6.4947 | 62% |
| 4 | 8.2412 | 3.9120 | +4.329 | 9.5434 | 86% |
| 5 | 11.5307 | 5.1591 | +6.372 | 11.9557 | 96% |
| **6** | **12.7235** | 5.3650 | **+7.359** | **12.7726** | **99.6%** |

- **H1**: the additive deficit grows MONOTONICALLY (synergy compounds without bound short of the ceiling).
- **H2**: every marginal reproduces its paper of origin.
- **H3**: the 6-dial which-factor wall reads 0.3594 vs permutation-null 0.3591 (**z = +0.11**) — sparse-bias-dominated as at k=4; factor-blindness extends to k=6.

### The battery-capacity law
1. I(k-joint) → H(joint labels): the CRT-joint modulus sees all k residues simultaneously; the pair-label structure becomes nearly fully determined (99.6% at k=6).
2. D(k) grows monotonically: marginal bookkeeping understates batteries progressively (7.36 bits = 3.7× additive at k=6).
3. The ceiling is the joint label entropy — population correlation between label blocks is all that remains.

### Method notes disclosed
Row-label off-by-one in the printout (cosmetic, corrected here); chained label code ~10¹² values requires np.unique-based entropy (bincount would allocate 5.6 TiB).

Now 429 experiments. Assessment v205. Paper 94.
